title: Recovery and Plasticity Simulator
summary: Watch five simulated people recover over twenty-four months, then take one rising score apart into restitution, relearning, compensation and practice. Compare it with a task the person never trained.
learningObjectives: Name four processes that all raise a score after an injury and say how they differ.
Explain why a single trained-task score cannot separate them.
State what an untrained task, an alternate test form and an untreated comparison group each rule out.
Read a fan of trajectories rather than a single curve, and judge whether a month-to-month change means anything.
Explain why compensation is a real gain and still not restored function.
interactionTypes: presets that converge on the same score
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab. Nothing here is a prognosis and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native range, radio and button controls, each with an accessible name; every slider carries a meaningful aria-valuetext in words, such as 'Injury severity 5 of 10, moderate, starting capacity 55 points' and '9 months after the injury'. All three charts are hidden from assistive technology and each carries a visible sentence inside its own figure giving the same information in numbers, and each is paired with a table. Nothing depends on colour: the five trajectories have five different dash patterns and each prints its own label at the right-hand end, the trained and untrained lines are solid and dashed and both are labelled, the month marker is a dotted rule labelled with its month number, and the five segments of the decomposition bar are named in left-to-right order with their values in the sentence underneath. Each experiment has its own pinned primary and the inactive one is hidden; measured at 1366 by 768 the pins are 355px and 264px, and with the last control of experiment 1 scrolled to the bottom of the window the fan is still at the top of the stage. Nothing animates, so there is no motion to reduce. Every slider, preset and redraw announces through the shell's polite live region, and focus moves to the simulator heading when the prediction unlocks it. Wide tables scroll inside their own containers, heading levels do not skip, forced colours are handled, and there is no horizontal page scroll at 320px, 375px, 1366px, 1440px or 1920px. The first stage shows one slider - when the measurement is taken. The injury severity and rehabilitation intensity that produced the curve sit behind a disclosure, as do the measurement noise and the other four people. Controls held back sit inside native <details> elements, reachable by keyboard in one step and announced as collapsed rather than being disabled.
readmeTopic: Why four different processes all look like getting better, and what evidence separates recovered function from a better strategy
simulationNotes: An invented model, not data. Severity s runs 1 to 10; capacity just after the injury is C0 = max(5, 100 - 9s) and lost = 100 - C0. Restitution has ceiling lost x (0.55 - 0.035s) and time constant 3 months; relearning has ceiling (lost - restitution ceiling) x rehabilitation intensity x max(0.15, 0.75 - 0.045s) and time constant 9 months; compensation has ceiling min(22, (0.25 x strategy use + 0.12 x environmental support) x lost) and time constant 6 months; practice effects add up to 6 points with time constant 4 months. The trained task is the sum of all five terms capped at 100; the untrained task is starting capacity plus restitution plus relearning, so the gap between the two curves is exactly compensation plus practice. The ceilings shrink as severity rises, so at severity 10 with every slider at maximum the trained task reaches 76 at 24 months and the untrained task 48 - plasticity is not unlimited. In experiment 1 each of five simulated people gets a restitution multiplier from 0.7 to 1.3, a relearning multiplier from 0.6 to 1.4 and a late drift of about N(0, 0.12) points per month after month 6, so some trajectories plateau and some fall; measurement noise is added at every month with SD 2, 5 or 9. Random numbers come from mulberry32 with a visible seed starting at 20260812 and advancing by 7919 on each redraw, with Box-Muller for the normal deviates. Reference values at 9 months, severity 5: Route A (rehabilitation 100 per cent, no compensation) gives trained 86 and untrained 80; Route B (no rehabilitation, strategy use 80 per cent, environmental support 60 per cent) gives trained 86 and untrained 71. Deliberate simplifications: four processes is a caricature and they overlap in time; real trajectories include illness, medication, mood, surgery and life events; rehabilitation is one slider standing for intensity, timing, content, specificity and motivation; no published trajectory, effect size or recovery rate is reproduced; no anatomy is named; and nothing here is a prognosis for anybody.
